summary: The paper delivers a rigorous, zero-O(.) non-asymptotic analysis of the Khanna-Putterman-Song deterministic linear-time MSF framework, uncovering a genuine 10^17-10^22 polylogarithmic factorial blowup in polynomial depth schedules and proving that geometric-horizon schedules converge across all five recursion series if and only if 1 < rho < kappa^(1/13). All combinatorial sharpenings—the tight 2t-1 bad-round ceiling, sharpened greedy portal bound, and exact pairwise Fredman extremality M(n,2) = floor((n^2+n+2)/3)—and every constant in the T*(m,n) <= 944m master bound (including base-case-free T_PICK(N) <= 23N, Claim 3.12 estimation, and directed Komlos verification) check out cleanly.
strengths: Exact combinatorial sharpenings in Theorem 1, notably the tight 2t-1 bad-round ceiling resolving t=1 degeneracy, the (2r^2-2r+1)/r^3 greedy portal bound, and the exact pairwise maxima-vector maximum M(n,2) = floor((n^2+n+2)/3) with 2/3 asymptotic separation from binomial(n+1,2).

Identification and zero-float certification of the factorial polylogarithmic blowup in KPS d^3 schedules alongside the sharp necessary-and-sufficient geometric stability domain 1 < rho < kappa^(1/13) and closed-form rational series bounds.

Complete zero-O(.) comparison accounting achieving T*(m,n) <= 944m, supported by a base-case-free T_PICK(N) <= 23N selection proof (with 6-comparison median-of-5 circuit for N >= 680 and merge sort for N < 680), unconditional Claim 3.12 estimation, and careful LCA splitting for directed Komlos verification.
Clear separation and transparent scoping between machine-checked constructive Lean 4.36.0 proofs, zero-float exact rational Python certificates, and cited external theorems from [7, 8, 9].
weaknesses: The underlying correctness of KPS Algorithm 1 (admissibility backward induction and Claim 3.12 sampling existence), Komlos's explicit directed verification bound [8, Theorem 1], and the Pettie-Ramachandran O(1) pointer-machine table-lookup translation [9] are imported rather than formalized from scratch in Lean.
The explicit 944m bound governs comparison complexity T*(m,n) rather than uniform pointer-machine running time, though Remark 1 states this scope explicitly.
